description: Live in-person stage presentations and panels at DEF CON 29, featuring live exploits, closing ceremonies, policy panels, badge making, and covert communications.

talks.title: Closing Ceremonies (Live)
talks.teaser: Jeff Moss (The Dark Tangent) and the DEF CON team wrap up DEF CON 29 in Las Vegas, announcing contest winners, CTF champions, and closing reflections.
talks.summary:
DEF CON Conference Presentation

This segment features remarks and presentations from DEF CON organizers and security leaders. Topics include the state of cybersecurity, hacker culture, community initiatives, and the conference's impact on the security landscape.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: PINATA: PIN Automatic Try Attack (Live)
talks.teaser: Salvador Mendoza presents the live demonstration of PINATA, an automated hardware rig executing rapid PIN brute-force attacks on flawed EMV smart cards.
talks.summary:
The Limits of EMV Smart Card Protections

While EMV payment cards enforce PIN Try Counters (PTC) to block brute force discovery, improper counter persistence across power resets creates critical attack vectors.

Demonstrating the PINATA Hardware Rig Live

Salvador Mendoza presents the live in-person demonstration of PINATA, an automated hardware attack rig that injects PIN attempts and cycles card power lines.

Bypassing Applet Retry Counters in Sub-Seconds

Mendoza demonstrates exhausting 4-digit PIN keyspaces on vulnerable banking applets, illustrating why cards must enforce non-volatile write updates.

Remediation for Payment Applet Developers

The author provides banking institutions and smart card manufacturers with secure non-volatile memory transaction standards.

talks.title: Ransomware's Big Year: From Nuisance to Scourge (Live Panel)
talks.teaser: Former White House officials and policy leaders debate the escalation of ransomware from financial nuisance to full-scale national security scourge.
talks.summary:
The Transformation of Ransomware into National Crisis

Following catastrophic attacks on Colonial Pipeline and JBS, cyber extortion transitioned from opportunistic cybercrime into a premier national security threat.

Evaluating Federal Policy and Regulatory Responses

Panelists debate government interventions—including mandatory incident disclosure, cryptocurrency tracing, and potential bans on ransom payments.

International Law Enforcement and Offensive Disruption

The discussion explores coordinated international law enforcement operations, economic sanctions on illicit crypto exchanges, and military cyber operations.

A Comprehensive Strategy for Critical Infrastructure Defense

The panel outlines necessary reforms for public-private resilience, threat intelligence sharing, and defensive subsidies for municipal targets.

talks.title: Hackers into the UN: Cyber Discussions on War and Peace (Live Policy Panel)
talks.teaser: International cyber diplomats and researchers discuss United Nations negotiations on state behavior, cyber warfare norms, and civilian protections.
talks.summary:
The Geopolitics of International Cyber Norms

Amidst global supply chain hacks and attacks on pandemic response infrastructure, the United Nations Group of Governmental Experts (UN GGE) and Open-Ended Working Group (OEWG) debate state cyber behavior.

Bridging the Technical Community and Global Diplomacy

Panelists discuss how technical cybersecurity experts and civil society organizations can participate in UN diplomatic processes.

Defining Red Lines for State-Sponsored Cyber Operations

The panel examines international humanitarian law in cyberspace, focusing on prohibitions against targeting critical civilian hospitals, power grids, and water systems.

Fostering Global Cyber Peace and Accountability

The speakers explore mechanisms for independent international attribution, treaty compliance verification, and promoting open internet governance.

talks.title: Rebooting Critical Infrastructure Protection (Live Panel)
talks.teaser: Cyber leaders evaluate 23 years of US Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) policy, assessing public-private partnerships and regulatory reform.
talks.summary:
Evaluating Two Decades of Critical Infrastructure Policy

Since Presidential Decision Directive 63 in 1998, governments worldwide have relied on voluntary Public-Private Partnerships to protect critical national infrastructure.

The Limits of Voluntary Information Sharing

Panelists analyze why voluntary frameworks have struggled to prevent systemic disruptions across energy grids, pipelines, and healthcare systems.

The Shift Toward Mandatory Regulatory Standards

The discussion explores emerging regulatory mandates, TSA pipeline directives, and national cyber performance goals for critical infrastructure sectors.

A New Paradigm for Societal Resilience

The panel advocates for fundamental structural changes—including civil liability reform, software bill of materials (SBOM) mandates, and out-of-band operational overrides.

talks.title: Attacking from Above: The Legal & Technical Battle for the Sky (Live)
talks.teaser: MAVSH breaks down the regulatory and technical battles over FAA Remote Identification rules, exploring drone privacy and hobbyist aviation rights.
talks.summary:
The Escalating Regulatory Conflict in Unmanned Aviation

Drone hobbyists and model aviation enthusiasts have been locked in high-stakes legal battles with the FAA over new airspace regulations.

Deconstructing FAA Remote Identification (Remote ID)

MAVSH provides an in-depth technical and legal analysis of the FAA Remote ID mandate, which requires drones to continuously broadcast operator location.

Privacy, Safety, and Economic Implications for Pilots

The author examines how broadcasting pilot GPS coordinates in real time creates physical safety risks, stalking vectors, and burdensome compliance costs.

Technical Defenses and Legal Advocacy

The presentation explores open-source firmware options, legal challenges, and community advocacy strategies to preserve hobbyist flying freedom.

talks.title: Hacking G Suite: The Power of Dark Apps Script Magic (Live)
talks.teaser: Matthew Bryant demonstrates post-exploitation magic in Google Workspace (G Suite), abusing Google Apps Script triggers to harvest credentials and pivot.
talks.summary:
Google Workspace as an Under-Audited Enterprise Target

While Google Cloud Platform (GCP) receives extensive security scrutiny, Google Workspace (formerly G Suite) contains powerful embedded scripting engines that remain overlooked.

Weaponizing Google Apps Script for Post-Exploitation

Matthew Bryant demonstrates how attackers abuse Google Apps Script triggers, Gmail add-ons, and Docs macros to execute serverless payloads inside Google's infrastructure.

Silent Data Exfiltration and Lateral Movement

By leveraging Apps Script's native permissions, an implant can read all corporate emails, clone private Drive documents, and exfiltrate secrets without generating endpoint EDR telemetry.

Hardening Google Workspace Environments

Bryant provides Workspace administrators with API restriction policies, third-party app allowlists, and logging strategies to detect malicious script executions.

talks.title: DoS: Denial of Shopping - Analyzing and Exploiting Physical Shopping Carts
talks.teaser: Joseph Gabay reverse engineers supermarket anti-theft perimeter wheel locks, spoofing low-frequency RF control signals to lock and unlock shopping carts.
talks.summary:
The Physical Perimeter Defenses of Retail Shopping Carts

Supermarkets and commercial shopping centers deploy electronic perimeter-locking caster wheels to prevent shopping carts from leaving parking lots.

Reverse Engineering Anti-Theft RF Wheel Locks

Joseph Gabay analyzes the low-frequency RF signals, underground perimeter loop transmitters, and optical triggers used to command cart wheel locking mechanisms.

Capturing, Replaying, and Spoofing Lock Signals

Using low-cost software-defined radios and microcontrollers, Gabay demonstrates capturing and replaying the unencrypted locking and unlocking radio codes.

Designing Secure Contactless Physical Perimeter Systems

The author discusses the complete absence of cryptographic authentication in physical retail deterrence devices and presents design improvements.

talks.title: A Look Inside Security at The New York Times (Live)
talks.teaser: New York Times information security analyst Jesse 'Agent X' Krembs presents live insights into protecting investigative journalists and confidential sources.
talks.summary:
The Frontline Defense of Investigative Journalism

Major global news organizations operate in a hostile threat environment, facing advanced nation-state adversaries, surveillance actors, and online harassment campaigns.

Operational Tradecraft for Source Protection

Jesse Krembs discusses defensive protocols used by investigative reporters in the field, including air-gapped computers, secure drop platforms, and encrypted messaging.

Hard Technical Challenges in Modern Media Defense

The presentation examines technical engineering hurdles—securing remote newsrooms, protecting reporters crossing hostile borders, and auditing zero-click mobile exploits.

Collaborating with the Hacker Community

Krembs invites security researchers to collaborate with journalistic organizations to strengthen open-source privacy tooling and defend free speech.

talks.title: Extension Land: Exploits and Rootkits in Browser Extensions (Live)
talks.teaser: Barak Sternberg delivers the live demonstration on weaponizing browser extension IPC and message-passing flaws into persistent browser rootkits.
talks.summary:
The Overlooked Attack Surface of Browser Extensions

Browser extensions enjoy high-privilege access across web origins, cookies, and local storage, often functioning outside standard browser security models.

Live Analysis of Extension IPC Vulnerabilities

Barak Sternberg examines message-passing and postMessage handlers in popular extensions, showing how unvalidated input allows malicious websites to hijack extension APIs.

Transforming Browser Extensions into Stealthy Rootkits

Sternberg demonstrates how a compromised extension provides persistent execution, intercepts plaintext keystrokes, steals authentication tokens, and bypasses CSP rules.

Defensive Manifest Architecture and Auditing

The author provides developers with secure coding standards for Manifest V3, input validation routines, and tools to audit extension attack surfaces.

talks.title: You're Doing IoT RNG Wrong (Live)
talks.teaser: Dan Petro and Allan Cecil present their live research on broken hardware Random Number Generators across IoT chipsets, extracting static zero-keys.
talks.summary:
The Critical Role of Randomness in Embedded Cryptography

Cryptographic operations on IoT microcontrollers—including key generation and session nonces—depend on hardware Random Number Generators for mathematical security.

Live Demonstration of Hardware RNG Failures

Dan Petro and Allan Cecil demonstrate how flawed driver integration and uninitialized silicon registers cause IoT devices to generate predictable, static zero-value encryption keys.

Auditing Hardware Silicon and Firmware Stacks

The authors review entropy harvesting routines across major microcontroller vendors, highlighting architectural shortcuts that compromise randomness.

Verified Implementation Guidelines for Hardware Engineers

Petro and Cecil outline verified methodologies for combining analog hardware noise with cryptographically secure PRNGs.

talks.title: New Phishing Attacks Exploiting OAuth Authentication Flows (Live)
talks.teaser: Jenko Hwong demonstrates live phishing attacks exploiting OAuth 2.0 device authorization flows, bypassing MFA and hijacking cloud session tokens.
talks.summary:
The Mechanics of OAuth 2.0 Device Flow Phishing

OAuth 2.0 device authorization allows limited-input devices (such as smart TVs) to authenticate via a short user code entered on a phone or computer.

Live Exploitation of Device Code Authentication

Jenko Hwong demonstrates crafting deceptive phishing campaigns where victim users authenticate legitimate login prompts, unknowingly authorizing the attacker's session.

Bypassing Multi-Factor Authentication and Consent Prompts

Because authentication occurs directly on the legitimate identity provider domain, MFA is satisfied and token grants give attackers persistent API access without hosting phishing infrastructure.

Detection, Mitigation, and Token Governance

The author releases open-source auditing tools and provides identity architects with detection strategies for anomalous device code grants.

talks.title: Community Panel: DEF CON 102 (Live)
talks.teaser: Jeff Moss (The Dark Tangent) and community veterans host an ad-hoc DEF CON 102 panel, sharing convention lore, survival tips, and hacker culture.
talks.summary:
This DEF CON talk covers community panel: def con 102 (live).

talks.title: Making the DEF CON 29 Badge (Live)
talks.teaser: Badge creators Michael and Katie Whiteley join The Dark Tangent on stage to share the engineering, chip shortage hurdles, and puzzles of the DC29 badge.
talks.summary:
The Journey of Designing the DEF CON 29 Badge

Creating the official electronic badge for DEF CON 29 required overcoming global semiconductor shortages, manufacturing shutdowns, and pandemic logistics.

Live Hardware Teardown and Circuit Architecture

Michael and Katie Whiteley walk through the custom circuit board design, power management constraints, and LED matrix display hardware.

Embedded Firmware and Challenge Puzzles

The designers discuss the embedded microcontroller firmware, communication protocols, and multi-stage interactive cryptographic puzzle game built into the badge.

Community Maker Lessons and Hardware Resiliency

The session provides hardware hackers and makers with practical lessons in component substitution, rapid prototyping, and embedded software testing.

talks.title: SPARROW: A Novel Covert Communication Scheme (Live)
talks.teaser: Reza Soosahabi and Chuck McAuley demonstrate live covert data transmission over cellular networks, exploiting MAC-layer protocols in LTE and 5G.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of Covert Cellular Communications

While wireless security research often focuses on creating custom PHY-layer radios, existing cellular infrastructures provide overlooked protocol channels for stealthy communication.

Discovering the MAC-Layer Vulnerability (GSMA CVD-2021-0045)

Reza Soosahabi and Chuck McAuley detail a protocol vulnerability in LTE and 5G MAC-layer signaling that enables covert, long-range communication across public carrier networks.

Live Demonstration of SPARROW Covert Devices

The authors present live testing of SPARROW devices transmitting covert messages over commercial cellular infrastructure without establishing active data sessions.

Detection Mechanisms and Carrier Defenses

Soosahabi and McAuley propose carrier-level traffic inspection heuristics and base station firmware updates to detect and mitigate unauthorized MAC-layer signaling.
